standard_prerequisites: Same chapter: lemma-relatively-prime-polynomials (two polynomials over a field are relatively prime exactly when they share no root in an algebraic closure); separability of a polynomial as coprimality with its derivative
core_obligations: If alpha is a common root of P and P', write P = (x - alpha)Q so P' = Q + (x - alpha)Q', whence alpha is a root of Q and (x - alpha)^2 divides P: not pairwise distinct roots
Conversely a repeated root (x - alpha)^2 | P makes alpha a root of both P and P'
Coupled with lemma-relatively-prime-polynomials (no common root iff relatively prime) this gives separable iff pairwise distinct roots
proof_roadmap: Pass from a common root to a double root by one differentiation
Run the converse and close with the coprimality criterion
